old: You, Indra, with your own help, are the protector of us, of the people who long for you. You are the lord and protector of the giver, who, truly devout in thought, draws near to you.

why: reviewer (minor): itthā-dhī: "devout" is an addition; Hindi says only "सच्चे चिन्तन वाला"; dhī = thought in the glossary. English, Hindi and gloss disagree.

old: truly devout, right in thought

why: reviewer (minor): Same: "truly devout" is interpretation.

old: Him, Indra, I praise; him I extol, in whom of old they grew strong and prevailed. May he, coming, fulfil the wish for wealth of the new man who seeks to make hymns.

old: He, Indra, the Vṛtra-slayer, the fort-destroyer, scattered the black-wombed female Dāsas. He brought forth earth and waters for man, and wholly urged on the praise of the sacrificer.
